purpose: Cartoon dinosaur fossil art and inventory cell-footprint concept

assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE polished cartoon GAME BACKPACK INVENTORY SCREEN, not a sheet of equal square item icons. Use the supplied picture ONLY as the reference for the appealing cartoon dinosaur fossil art style, warm ivory bone, ochre shadows, brown contours and soft painted highlights. Build a completely new inventory composition.
MAIN REQUEST: a large straight-on 8-column by 8-row inventory made of clearly visible, perfectly equal SQUARE CELLS. Different dinosaur fossil bones physically span DIFFERENT NUMBERS OF THESE CELLS, like a grid-based item-size backpack. The artwork must make the size difference obvious: 1×2, 1×3, 1×4, 2×2, 2×3, 2×4 and 3×3 footprints. Do not put every bone in a 2×2 square.
View is strictly orthographic, all grid lines precisely horizontal and vertical, NO perspective tilt. All objects' main axes are vertical or horizontal, never placed diagonally or turned 30/45 degrees. Natural curved anatomy is fine; do not stretch or squash anatomy to fill cells. Each occupied rectangle has a very subtle olive/ochre slot tint and a thin rectangular footprint outline, with the underlying square cell divisions still visible enough to count. No oversized empty padding around individual bones. Keep bone art entirely inside its assigned footprint.
Layout, using columns 1–8 left-to-right and rows 1–8 top-to-bottom:
- column 1, rows 1–4: one genuinely tall narrow DINOSAUR LEG BONE, a 1×4 item; rounded full-size joints and a long straight shaft, vertical.
- column 2, rows 1–3: an articulated chain of chunky DINOSAUR SPINE VERTEBRAE, a 1×3 item; vertical.
- column 3, rows 1–2: a short chunky DINOSAUR TOE/LIMB BONE, a 1×2 item; vertical.
- columns 4–5, rows 1–2: a horizontal-facing TYRANNOSAUR SKULL, a 2×2 item.
- columns 6–7, rows 1–3: a medium DINOSAUR RIB CAGE with a vertical spine and 4–5 pairs of ribs, a 2×3 item.
- columns 1–2, rows 5–8: a distinctly taller DINOSAUR RIB CAGE with a vertical spine and 7 pairs of ribs, a 2×4 item.
- columns 4–6, rows 5–7: a wide connected DINOSAUR PELVIS FOSSIL, a large 3×3 item.
- columns 4–7, row 4: a connected tapering DINOSAUR TAIL VERTEBRA CHAIN, placed horizontally in a 4×1 footprint.
- columns 4–6, row 8: a long DINOSAUR LOWER JAW with a row of teeth, placed horizontally in a 3×1 footprint.
- column 8, rows 5–7: an articulated long RAPTOR TOE AND SICKLE CLAW, vertical in a 1×3 footprint.
Leave the remaining cells visibly empty. No overlapping item footprints. Every item is a DINOSAUR SKELETAL FOSSIL, never human bones or living dinosaurs.
Add a small neat cream size tag such as “1×4”, “1×3”, “1×2”, “2×2”, “2×3”, “2×4”, “3×3” in the bottom corner of each occupied rectangle, with clear legible type. A modest top title “恐龙化石背包”. Frame: tasteful prehistoric hide-and-wood game inventory frame, dark desaturated olive/brown slot interiors for good ivory-bone contrast; thin clear slot dividers. The grid dominates the entire image. Minimal top header, no extra currencies, controls, status bars, character portraits, decorative objects or UI clutter.
High-quality hand-painted CARTOON mobile-game art, friendly chunky silhouettes with subtle bone cracks; not photorealistic, not a sterile geometric diagram, not a website, not an equal-size icon gallery. Make the single-cell-width long bones visibly slender, and the 3×3 pelvis visibly massive by comparison. Square or slightly portrait full-screen composition with clean uniform grid geometry.

assets.style: thick brown outline, flat ivory/tan fills, cream square grid and stitched leather frame
assets.prompt:
Edit image 1, which is the target dinosaur-bone inventory drawing. Image 2 is only the original game's STYLE REFERENCE.
Keep the successful simple flat ivory/tan bone colors, thick slightly wobbly dark-brown outlines, cream sticker rims, simplified cartoon bone drawings and thin stitched brown frame from image 1. Keep the reference game's restrained flat illustration style. Do not add shiny rendering, realistic cracks, gradients, 3D bone material, a title banner, text headers, rocks, fruit, reward bubbles or unrelated objects.

Make ONE targeted correction: rebuild the inventory's underlying grid and repack these same bone items so EVERY cell is a TRUE EQUAL-SIZED SQUARE. There must be exactly SEVEN columns and NINE rows, like the portrait reference game's grid, straight front-on view with no perspective. All 63 individual square tiles have precisely the same width and height; no half-height extra rows, no thin strip tiles along top/bottom, no elongated rectangles masquerading as cells. A portrait panel with ratio close to 7:9 plus its narrow leather stitched border will naturally fit this grid. Thin warm-ochre square-tile divisions must remain visible under each item's rectangle so the cells can be counted. No text except the small size tags.
The bones' main axes stay strictly horizontal or vertical, with natural proportions. The different inventory footprints must occupy exact integer numbers of these equal square cells. Keep each drawing fully inside its footprint with a little margin. No overlapping footprints.

Place items on the 7-by-9 square grid, with row 1 at the TOP:
- col 1, rows 1–4: slender long dinosaur leg bone, VERTICAL 1×4.
- col 2, rows 1–3: dinosaur spine vertebra chain, VERTICAL 1×3.
- col 3, rows 1–2: a short dinosaur limb/toe bone, VERTICAL 1×2.
- cols 4–5, rows 1–2: simplified T-rex skull in side view, HORIZONTAL jaw line, 2×2.
- cols 6–7, rows 1–3: medium connected dinosaur rib cage, VERTICAL spine, 2×3.
- cols 3–6, row 4: tapering dinosaur tail vertebra chain, HORIZONTAL 4×1.
- cols 1–2, rows 5–8: tall connected dinosaur rib cage, VERTICAL spine, 2×4.
- cols 3–5, rows 5–7: wide dinosaur pelvis, 3×3.
- col 7, rows 5–7: articulated raptor toe and sickle claw, VERTICAL 1×3, soft light-green slot tint.
- cols 3–5, row 8: dinosaur lower jaw with teeth, HORIZONTAL 3×1.
Leave the other cells, including the whole ninth row, EMPTY. Small unobtrusive dark-brown size tags “1×4”, “1×3”, “1×2”, “2×2”, “2×3”, “2×4”, “3×3”, “4×1”, “3×1” should agree with the actual square-grid footprints.
The result should look like the attached reference game's simple flat hand-drawn inventory board filled with mixed-size dinosaur fossils, with clean square-cell geometry.
assets.base_prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / stylized-concept.
Create ONE new DINOSAUR FOSSIL INVENTORY BOARD image closely matching the VISUAL STYLE of the attached game screenshot.
Input image 1 is the STYLE REFERENCE: copy its flat, simple, slightly rough hand-drawn game illustration language, muted cream/brown palette, bold dark chocolate contours, parchment cell tiles, stitched leather edging, tiny sparse flecks, small flat item shadows and sticker-like item readability. Change the contents to dinosaur bones. This is a new art variant, not a reproduction of the rocks/fruits in the reference.

STYLE MATCH IS THE HIGHEST PRIORITY:
- Simple charming 2D cartoon icons with thick dark-brown slightly uneven outlines.
- Flat cream/ivory bone fill, one muted tan shadow shape and at most one small off-white highlight shape. Very restrained color count, no tonal gradients or smooth 3D modeling.
- Slightly lumpy organic shapes and simplified anatomy, drawn with the same chunky pen feel as the rock icons in the reference.
- A subtle thin cream sticker rim around each bone group, like the inventory items in the reference.
- Absolutely no glossy golden fossils, ornate realistic rendering, shiny bevels, detailed cracks, painterly brush texture, bloom, realistic lighting or photographic textures.
- No pixel grid/pixel art aesthetic; use the reference's simple slightly rough outline illustration.

COMPOSITION:
A front-facing backpack grid fills almost the whole portrait image. Exactly 8 columns by 8 rows of equal SQUARE cream parchment cells, softly rounded individual tile corners, thin muted ochre separators. Compact brown leather frame with a thin ivory dashed stitch along the inside, closely matching the supplied screenshot. No enormous header, no decorative wooden logs, no 3D frame, no background scenery. Keep the grid straight and flat with no perspective.
The items occupy different rectangular numbers of grid cells: 1×2, 1×3, 1×4, 2×2, 2×3, 2×4 and 3×3. Occupied footprints remain visible as unobtrusive thin brown outlines or very faint slot tint, with underlying square tile subdivisions visible enough to count. One small vertical item may have a muted light-green selected slot like the reference.
Each bone's main axis is exactly VERTICAL or HORIZONTAL, never diagonal. Naturally curved anatomy is allowed, but no object rotation or nonuniform stretching. Long bones have genuinely long narrow shafts with naturally round full-size joints. Different lengths of spine come from different numbers of articulated vertebrae. Do not make everything a 2×2 icon.

EXACT INVENTORY CONTENTS AND PLACEMENT (columns left to right, rows top to bottom):
1. Column 1, rows 1–4: one slender long dinosaur femur, upright, 1×4.
2. Column 2, rows 1–3: upright chain of dinosaur back vertebrae, 1×3.
3. Column 3, rows 1–2: short chunky dinosaur limb/toe bone, upright, 1×2.
4. Columns 4–5, rows 1–2: a recognizable simplified Tyrannosaurus skull side view, jaws horizontal, 2×2.
5. Columns 6–7, rows 1–3: medium connected dinosaur rib cage, spine vertical, 2×3.
6. Columns 1–2, rows 5–8: taller connected dinosaur rib cage with more ribs, vertical, 2×4.
7. Columns 4–6, rows 5–7: wide chunky dinosaur pelvis with two large open holes, 3×3.
8. Columns 4–7, row 4: a tapering dinosaur tail vertebra chain, horizontal, 4×1.
9. Columns 4–6, row 8: dinosaur lower jaw with a row of simple teeth, horizontal, 3×1.
10. Column 8, rows 5–7: articulated raptor toe ending in a sickle claw, upright, 1×3.
Leave other cells EMPTY so the grid system is obvious. No overlap between items. A tiny dark-brown “1×4”, “1×3”, “1×2”, “2×2”, “2×3”, “2×4”, “3×3”, “4×1” or “3×1” footprint label may appear at the bottom corner of each item rectangle, discreetly integrated rather than in big shiny UI plaques.
All items are DINOSAUR SKELETAL BONES. No human bones, rocks, vines, fruit, treasure chests, currency, reward bubbles, energy symbols, characters or miscellaneous objects. No extra buttons or interface clutter. The image should look like the same artists who drew the attached reference made a dinosaur-bone backpack with mixed-size items.
